label: thmA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thmA}
Let $p$ be odd and $H$ a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and class
$c\le p-2$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item every $\alpha\in\operatorname{UAut}(\mathbb{F}_p H)$ acts on $V$ exactly as the group
automorphism $\exp(\mu)$ does, for some $\mu\in\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H))$;
\item the commutator sector $C(V)=V\cap[E,E]$ is canonically isomorphic to
$H_2(\mathfrak l(H))$, the group $U(H)$ acts faithfully on it, and
\[
U(H)=\exp\Bigl(\Omega\bigl(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H))\bigr)\Bigr)\ \le\
GL\bigl(H_2(\mathfrak l(H))\bigr),\qquad
|U(H)|=p^{\,\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\Omega(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H)))};
\]
\item $U(H)=1$ if and only if every derivation of positive degree of
$\mathfrak l(H)$ acts trivially on $H_2(\mathfrak l(H))$;
\item if $\mathfrak l(H)$ is graded, then non-isomorphic central Frattini extensions
of $H$ have non-isomorphic small group rings.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: thmB
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thmB}
Let $p\ge5$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item \textup{(one layer)} If $H_2(\mathfrak l(H))$ is concentrated in a single
degree, then $U(H)=1$. This covers the relatively free groups
$F_d/\gamma_{c+1}(F_d)F_d^{\,p}$ for all $d\ge2$ and $2\le c\le p-2$, in
particular the extraspecial group $p^{1+2}_+$ of order $p^3$ and exponent
$p$.
\item \textup{(two generators)} If $H=F_2/\gamma_{c+1}(F_2)F_2^{\,p}N$ with
$3\le c\le p-2$ and $N\le\gamma_c(F_2)$, then $U(H)=1$; in particular this
holds for the group of maximal class, order $p^4$ and exponent $p$.
\item \textup{(class two)} If $H$ has class $2$ and exponent $p$, with
$L_1=H/\Phi(H)$, $L_2=H'$ and commutator map $\omega:\Lambda^2L_1\to L_2$,
then $U(H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_1,L_2)/\ker\Omega$ is elementary abelian, every element of
it is realized by a central automorphism of $H$, and $\ker\Omega$ contains the
inner derivations. For the Heisenberg group $\operatorname{Heis}(p^n)$, the Sylow
$p$-subgroup of $SL_3(p^n)$, and for the direct power $(p^{1+2}_+)^M$ one has
$|U(H)|=p^{2n(n-1)}$, respectively $p^{2M(M-1)}$.
\end{enumerate}
In all these cases non-isomorphic central Frattini extensions of $H$ have
non-isomorphic small group rings.
head: environment

label: lem:grrigid
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:grrigid}
Let $\Theta:KG\to K\widetilde G$ be a $K$-algebra isomorphism. Then
$\operatorname{gr}\Theta:u(L(G))\to u(L(\widetilde G))$ maps $L_n(G)$ onto
$L_n(\widetilde G)$ for every $n$, compatibly with brackets and $p$-th
powers.
head: environment
name: graded rigidity

title: Proof
body_md:
$\Theta$ preserves the radical, hence the powers $\mathrm{I}^n$, so $\operatorname{gr}\Theta$ is an
isomorphism of graded algebras; it maps $L_1(G)=\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2$ onto
$L_1(\widetilde G)$, hence the restricted Lie subalgebra generated by
$L_1(G)$, which is $L(G)$, onto $L(\widetilde G)$, preserving degrees,
brackets and $p$-th powers (these being the associative ones).
head: environment

label: thm:HS
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:HS}
Isomorphism classes of extensions in $\mathcal F(H)$ correspond to
$\rho(\operatorname{Out}(H))$-orbits of subspaces of $V$, and isomorphism classes of the
pairs $(s(G,A),\{A-1\})$ correspond to $\rho(\operatorname{Out}(KH))$-orbits.
head: environment

label: lem:welldef
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:welldef}
The action of $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(KH)$ on $V$ does not depend on the lift.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Two lifts differ by an element of $\operatorname{Hom}(H/\Phi(H),V)$ \cite[Rem.~4.5]{HS07},
acting on the images $\hat x_i\in E\subset s^\times$ of a free basis by
$\hat x_i\mapsto\hat x_iv_i$ with $v_i\in V$ central. If $v$ is the class of
a relator $r$ then $r(\hat x_1v_1,\dots)=r(\hat x)\prod_iv_i^{e_i(r)}$, where
$e_i(r)$ is the exponent sum of $r$ in $x_i$; now $r\in\Phi(F)$ gives
$p\mid e_i(r)$, and $V$ is elementary abelian.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
$U(H)$ is the image of $\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ in $GL(V)$. The \emph{Levi factorization}
is the statement $\operatorname{Aut}(KH)=\operatorname{Aut}(H)\cdot\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$; it holds if and only if
the images of $\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ and of $\operatorname{Aut}(KH)$ in $GL(H/\Phi(H))=GL(\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2)$
coincide.
head: environment

label: lem:reform
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:reform}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item For $\alpha\in\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ and $v\in W_n$ one has
$v^\alpha v^{-1}\in W_{n+1}$; in particular $U(H)$ is a $p$-group of
unipotent transformations stabilizing the depth flag.
\item $\rho(\operatorname{Out}(KH))\supseteq\rho(\operatorname{Out}(H))\cdot U(H)$, with equality under
the Levi factorization.
\item If the Levi factorization holds and every element of $U(H)$ lies in
$\rho(\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{Aut}(H)\to\operatorname{Out}(KH)))$, then $\rho(\operatorname{Out}(KH))=\rho(\operatorname{Out}(H))$, and
for $G,\widetilde G\in\mathcal F(H)$ an isomorphism of pairs
$(s(G,A),\{A-1\})\cong(s(\widetilde G,\widetilde A),\{\widetilde A-1\})$
implies $G\cong\widetilde G$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) $\hat\alpha$ preserves $\mathrm{I}(s)^n$ and $\{V-1\}$, hence each $\{W_n-1\}$ by
\eqref{eq:PS}; since $(\hat\alpha-1)\mathrm{I}^n\subseteq\mathrm{I}^{n+1}$, on $\{W_n-1\}$
this reads $\{v^\alpha-1\}-\{v-1\}=\{v^\alpha v^{-1}-1\}\in\mathrm{I}^{n+1}$, that
is, $v^\alpha v^{-1}\in W_{n+1}$. (2) Group automorphisms extend to $KH$,
and under the Levi factorization every class of $\operatorname{Out}(KH)$ is a class of
$\operatorname{Out}(H)$ times a class of $\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$. (3) is (2) together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:HS}.
head: environment

label: lem:Omega
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Omega}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item Any two automorphisms of $\mathfrak e$ preserving $\mathfrak v$ and inducing the same
automorphism of $\mathfrak l$ agree on $\mathfrak v$; the same holds for derivations of $\mathfrak e$
preserving $\mathfrak v$ and inducing the same derivation of $\mathfrak l$.
\item Consequently $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathfrak l)$ acts on $\mathfrak v$, and there is a homomorphism of
Lie algebras $\Omega:\operatorname{Der}(\mathfrak l)\to\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak v)$, $\Omega(\mu)=\tilde\mu|_\mathfrak v$.
\item Inner derivations lie in $\ker\Omega$.
\item If $\Theta=\exp(\tilde\mu)\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathfrak e)$ for a lift $\tilde\mu$ of a
nilpotent $\mu\in\operatorname{Der}(\mathfrak l)$ with $\exp(\mu)$ defined, then
$\Theta|_\mathfrak v=\exp(\Omega(\mu))$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) If $\Theta_1,\Theta_2$ are such automorphisms then
$\Theta_1^{-1}\Theta_2$ is $x\mapsto x+\phi(x)$ with $\phi:\mathfrak e\to\mathfrak v$, and
since $\mathfrak v$ is central, $\phi([x,y])=0$; as $\mathfrak v\subseteq\gamma_2(\mathfrak e)$
(because $\mathfrak r\subseteq\gamma_2(\mathfrak f)$), $\phi$ vanishes on $\mathfrak v$. For
derivations, the difference is a derivation $\delta$ of $\mathfrak e$ with values in
$\mathfrak v$, whence $\delta[x,y]=[\delta x,y]+[x,\delta y]=0$ and $\delta$
vanishes on $\gamma_2(\mathfrak e)\supseteq\mathfrak v$. (2) follows, using that
$[\tilde\mu,\tilde\mu']$ lifts $[\mu,\mu']$. (3) $\operatorname{ad}_x$ lifts to
$\operatorname{ad}_{\tilde x}$, which maps $\mathfrak r$ into $[\mathfrak f,\mathfrak r]$. (4) is immediate from
(1).
head: environment

label: prop:E
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:E}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $E$ has class $\le c+1\le p-1$, $\gamma_2(E)$ has exponent $p$, and
$g\mapsto g^p$ is a homomorphism $E\to V$ factoring through $H/\Phi(H)$; its
image $\mho_1(E)$ is spanned by the independent classes of
$x_1^p,\dots,x_d^p$, and
\[
V=C(V)\oplus\mho_1(E),\qquad \dim V=\dim C(V)+d .
\]
\item $D_n(E)=\gamma_n(E)\mho_1(E)$ for $n\le p$ and $D_{p+1}(E)=1$; hence
$W_p=\mho_1(E)$, $W_{p+1}=1$, and $W_n\cap C(V)=\gamma_n(E)\cap C(V)$ for
$n\le p$, with $W_p\cap C(V)=0$.
\item Put $E^\circ:=E/\mho_1(E)$ and $V^\circ:=V/\mho_1(E)\cong C(V)$. Then
$E^\circ$ has exponent $p$ and class $\le c+1$, and under the Lazard
correspondence $E^\circ\leftrightarrow\mathfrak e$, $V^\circ\leftrightarrow\mathfrak v$ and
$E^\circ/V^\circ=H\leftrightarrow\mathfrak l$; the depth filtration of $C(V)$
corresponds to the degree filtration of $\mathfrak v$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: structure of $E$ and $V$

label: eq:HP
title: Proof
body_md:
(1) As $E/V=H$ has class $c$, we get $\gamma_{c+1}(E)\le V$ central and $E$
of class $\le c+1<p$; also $g^p\in V$ for all $g$, so $\mho_1(E)\le V$ is
central and elementary abelian. Hall--Petrescu \cite[Thm.~9.4]{Khu98} gives,
for $a,b\in E$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:HP}
[a^p,b]=[a,b]^p\prod_{k=2}^{p}w_k^{\binom pk},\qquad
w_k\in\gamma_k(\langle a,[a,b]\rangle),
\end{equation}
where the left-hand side is $1$ ($a^p$ being central) and
$w_p\in\gamma_p(E)=1$. We show $\mho_1(\gamma_k(E))=1$ by downward induction
on $k\ge2$: for $a\in\gamma_{k-1}$ and $b\in E$, all the $w_k$ in
\eqref{eq:HP} lie in $\gamma_{k+1}(E)$, whose $p$-th powers are trivial by
induction, so $[a,b]^p=1$; and for $g,h\in\gamma_k$ one has
$(gh)^p=g^ph^p\prod w_k^{\binom pk}$ with $w_k\in\gamma_{2k}\subseteq
\gamma_{k+1}$, so $\gamma_k$ has exponent $p$. The same expansion for
$g,h\in E$, with $w_k\in\gamma_2(E)$ of exponent $p$ and $p\mid\binom pk$ for
$k<p$, shows that $g\mapsto g^p$ is a homomorphism; it kills $\gamma_2(E)$
and $\mho_1(E)$, hence factors through $H/\Phi(H)$, and its image is spanned
by the $x_i^p$. Since $R\gamma_2(F)=F^p\gamma_2(F)$ and the exponent vectors
of $L$ form $p^2\mathbb{Z}^d$, we get $\bar E'\cong(C_{p^2})^d$, in which the
$\bar x_i^p$ are independent; so the $x_i^p$ are independent, $\varphi$ is
injective on $\mho_1(E)$, and $V=C(V)\oplus\mho_1(E)$.

(2) By \eqref{eq:jennings}, for $n\le p$ the relevant factors are
$\gamma_n(E)$ and $\mho_1(\gamma_1)=\mho_1(E)$, the others being trivial by
(1); for $n=p+1$ all factors are trivial. Since $\mho_1(E)\le V$ we get
$W_n=(V\cap\gamma_n(E))\mho_1(E)$ for $n\le p$; if $v\in C(V)\cap W_n$, write
$v=gu$ with $g\in V\cap\gamma_n$ and $u\in\mho_1(E)$, so that $g\in C(V)$ and
$u\in C(V)\cap\mho_1(E)=0$. Finally $\gamma_p(E)=1$.

(3) $E^\circ=F/[F,R]R^pF^p=F^\circ/[F^\circ,\bar R]$, where
$F^\circ=F/\gamma_{c+2}(F)F^p$ is relatively free of exponent $p$ and class
$c+1$ (note $\gamma_{c+2}(F)\le[F,\gamma_{c+1}(F)]\le[F,R]$ and
$R^p\le F^p$) and $\bar R$ is the image of $R$. By \S\ref{subsec:lazard},
$F^\circ\leftrightarrow\mathfrak f$, $\bar R\leftrightarrow\mathfrak r$ and
$[F^\circ,\bar R]\leftrightarrow[\mathfrak f,\mathfrak r]$, whence
$E^\circ\leftrightarrow\mathfrak e$ and
$V^\circ=\bar R/[F^\circ,\bar R]\leftrightarrow\mathfrak v$, with $\gamma_n$
corresponding to $\gamma_n$; by (2) the depth filtration of
$C(V)\cong V^\circ$ is $C(V)\cap\gamma_n(E)$.
head: environment

label: prop:absorb
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:absorb}
For every $\alpha\in\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ and every $v\in V$ one has
$v^\alpha v^{-1}\in C(V)$. Consequently $U(H)$ acts trivially on $V/C(V)$
and on $\mho_1(E)$, and $U(H)\to GL(C(V))$ is injective.
head: environment
name: displacements are commutators

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\bar V'=\varphi(V)$ and $A:=s(\bar E',\bar V')=K\bar E'/\mathrm{I}(K\bar V')
\mathrm{I}(K\bar E')$. Every element of $\bar V'$ is a $p$-th power in $\bar E'$,
because relators have exponent sums divisible by $p$; so
$\bar V'\le\mho_1(\bar E')=\Phi(\bar E')$ and
$(\bar E',\bar V')\in\mathcal F(H^{\mathrm{ab}})$, whence \eqref{eq:PS} holds
in $A$. Moreover $\varphi$ carries the generators $(v-1)(g-1)$ of
$\mathrm{I}(KV)\mathrm{I}(KE)$ to generators of the corresponding ideal over $\bar E'$, so it
induces an algebra morphism $\psi:s(E,V)\to A$ with
$\psi|_V=\varphi|_V$.

Let $\hat\alpha$ be a lift of $\alpha$, put
$\rho_i=\hat\alpha(\hat x_i)-\hat x_i$, which lies in $\mathrm{I}(s)^2$
\cite[Lem.~5.2]{HS07}, and $\sigma_i=\psi(\hat x_i)^{-1}\psi(\rho_i)\in
\mathrm{I}(A)^2$. Let $v\in V$ be the class of a relator $r$, so that
$v=r(\hat x_1,\dots,\hat x_d)$ and
$v^\alpha=r(u_1,\dots,u_d)$ with $u_i=\hat x_i(1+\hat x_i^{-1}\rho_i)$.
Applying $\psi$ and evaluating the word $r$ in the commutative algebra $A$ by
exponent sums,
\[
\psi(v^\alpha)=\prod_i\psi(\hat x_i)^{e_i(r)}\prod_i(1+\sigma_i)^{e_i(r)}
=\psi(v)\prod_i(1+\sigma_i)^{e_i(r)} .
\]
Since $\{V-1\}$ is a square-zero central ideal, $\delta:=v^\alpha v^{-1}$
satisfies $\varphi(\delta)=\psi(v^\alpha)\psi(v)^{-1}=\prod_i(1+\sigma_i)
^{e_i(r)}$. Now $H$ has exponent $p$, so $R\gamma_2(F)=F^p\gamma_2(F)$ and
every $e_i(r)$ is divisible by $p$, say $e_i(r)=pf_i$; as
$(1+\sigma)^p=1+\sigma^p$ in a commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra,
\[
\varphi(\delta)=\prod_i\bigl(1+\sigma_i^{\,p}\bigr)^{f_i},
\]
negative exponents being harmless since these are units. Hence
$\varphi(\delta)-1$ lies in the ideal generated by the
$\sigma_i^{\,p}\in\mathrm{I}(A)^{2p}$, so by \eqref{eq:PS} in $A$ we get
$\varphi(\delta)\in\bar V'\cap D_{2p}(\bar E')$. But
$\bar E'\cong(C_{p^2})^d$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:E}(1), and
$D_{2p}(\bar E')=\mho_2(\bar E')=1$ for an abelian group, since
$p<2p\le p^2$. Therefore $\varphi(\delta)=1$, that is
$\delta\in\ker(\varphi|_V)=C(V)$. Finally a source $v\in\mho_1(E)=W_p$ has
$v^\alpha v^{-1}\in W_{p+1}=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:reform}(1), and
$V=C(V)\oplus\mho_1(E)$.
head: environment

label: thm:dict
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dict}
Let $p$ be odd and $H$ of exponent $p$ and class $c\le p-2$. Under the
identifications of Proposition~\ref{prop:E}(3):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $C(V)\cong\mathfrak v\cong H_2(\mathfrak l(H))$, the depth flag corresponding to the
degree filtration; in particular the Schur multiplier $M(H)$ satisfies
$\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}M(H)/pM(H)=\dim H_2(\mathfrak l(H))$, and
$\dim H^2(H,\mathbb{F}_p)=\dim H_2(\mathfrak l(H))+d$;
\item for $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ with Lazard image $\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathfrak l)$, the
action $\rho(\beta)$ on $C(V)$ is the action of $\theta$ on $\mathfrak v$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:Omega}\textup{(2)}; if $\theta=\exp(\mu)$ with
$\mu\in\operatorname{Der}(\mathfrak l)$ nilpotent, then $\rho(\beta)|_{C(V)}=\exp(\Omega(\mu))$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: dictionary

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) The first assertion is Proposition~\ref{prop:E}(3) and Hopf's formula.
Since $R/(R\cap F')$ is free abelian, $R/[F,R]\cong M(H)\oplus\mathbb{Z}^d$, so
$V=(R/[F,R])\otimes\mathbb{F}_p$ has dimension $\dim H^2(H,\mathbb{F}_p)$ and $C(V)$, the image
of $R\cap F'$, is $M(H)/pM(H)$. (2) Lift $\beta$ to $F$; the induced
automorphism of $E$ descends to $E^\circ$ and corresponds to an automorphism
of $\mathfrak e$ preserving $\mathfrak v$ and inducing $\theta$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:Omega}(1),(4) apply.
head: environment

label: lem:log
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:log}
Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra with an ideal $I$ such that
$A=\mathbb{F}_p1\oplus I$ and $I^p=0$, and let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(A)$ satisfy
$(\alpha-1)(I)\subseteq I^2$. Put $N=\alpha-1$ and
$\Delta=\sum_{k=1}^{p-2}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}N^k$. Then $N^{p-1}=0$, the map
$\Delta$ is a derivation of $A$ with $\Delta(I^n)\subseteq I^{n+1}$, and
$\alpha=\exp\Delta:=\sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\Delta^k/k!$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, $N(I^n)\subseteq I^{n+1}$: write an element of $I^n$ as a sum of
products of $n$ elements of $I$ and expand $\alpha(a_1\cdots a_n)-
a_1\cdots a_n$ telescopically, each summand containing a factor
$N(a_j)\in I^2$. Hence $N^{p-1}(I)\subseteq I^p=0$, and $N(1)=0$. In
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}[t]/(t^{p-1})$ the truncated identities $\exp(\log(1+t))=1+t$ and
$\log(\exp t)=t$ hold, all denominators being prime to $p$; substituting
$t\mapsto N$ gives $\alpha=\exp\Delta$ and $\Delta^{p-1}=0$, as well as
$\Delta(I^n)\subseteq I^{n+1}$.

For the Leibniz rule, let $Q$ be the quotient of $I\otimes I$ by the subspace
$\sum_{i+j\ge p}I^i\otimes I^j$. The multiplication $m:I\otimes I\to A$
factors through $Q$, and the commuting operators $X=\Delta\otimes1$,
$Y=1\otimes\Delta$ act on $Q$ raising the total degree by one, so that every
monomial $X^aY^b$ with $a+b\ge p-1$ vanishes on $Q$. Hence, on $Q$,
\[
\alpha\otimes\alpha=\exp(X)\exp(Y)=\sum_{a+b\le p-2}\frac{X^aY^b}{a!\,b!}
=\exp(X+Y),
\]
the last equality because $\exp(X)\exp(Y)=\exp(X+Y)$ holds in
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}[X,Y]$ modulo total degree $p-1$. Put
$M':=\alpha\otimes\alpha-1$ on $Q$; then $M'=\exp(X+Y)-1$ with
$(X+Y)^{p-1}=0$, so $\log(1+M')=X+Y$ on $Q$. On the other hand
$m\circ M'=N\circ m$, because
$m((\alpha\otimes\alpha)(a\otimes b))=\alpha(ab)$; therefore
$m\circ M'^k=N^k\circ m$ for all $k$ and $m\circ\log(1+M')=\Delta\circ m$.
Thus $\Delta(ab)=m((X+Y)(a\otimes b))=\Delta(a)b+a\Delta(b)$ for
$a,b\in I$, and trivially when $a$ or $b$ is a scalar.
head: environment

label: lem:symm
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:symm}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $B=\mathbb{F}_p\oplus\mathfrak e\oplus\bigoplus_{j=2}^{p-1}\varepsilon_j(S^j\mathfrak e)$, every
summand is $\operatorname{ad}(\mathfrak e)$-stable, and the decomposition is compatible with the
$\mathrm{I}$-adic filtration: each $\mathrm{I}(B)^n$ is the sum of its intersections with
the summands, and $\mathrm{I}(B)^n\cap\mathfrak e=\gamma_n(\mathfrak e)$.
\item $J_B=\bigoplus_{j=2}^{p-1}\varepsilon_j(\mathfrak v\cdot S^{j-1}\mathfrak e)$, a sum of
$\operatorname{ad}(\mathfrak e)$-stable subspaces of the summands with $j\ge2$.
\item Consequently $s'=\mathbb{F}_p\oplus\mathfrak e\oplus C$ with $C$ $\operatorname{ad}(\mathfrak e)$-stable; the
group $E^\circ$ and the algebra $\mathfrak e$ embed in $s'$,
$\mathfrak e\cap\mathrm{I}(s')^n=\gamma_n(\mathfrak e)$, and the projection $p_1:s'\to\mathfrak e$ along
$\mathbb{F}_p\oplus C$ satisfies $p_1([u,b])=[p_1(u),b]$ for $u\in s'$, $b\in\mathfrak e$, as
well as $p_1(\mathrm{I}(s')^n)\subseteq\gamma_n(\mathfrak e)$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: symmetrization decomposition

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) Filter $S^j\mathfrak e$ by total degree, induced from the lower central
filtration of $\mathfrak e$, and let
$\varepsilon:\bigoplus_{j\le p-1}S^j\mathfrak e\to B$ be $\sum_j\varepsilon_j$, a
filtered map. Elements of degree $\ge p$ map into $\mathrm{I}(B)^p=0$, so
$\varepsilon$ factors through the quotient by degree $\ge p$. On associated
graded objects $\operatorname{gr}\varepsilon$ is the symmetrization
$\bigoplus_{j<p}S^jL\to u(L)/(\deg\ge p)$ with $L=L(E^\circ)$. By the
restricted Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt theorem \cite{Jac62} the length
filtration of $u(L)$ has associated graded $S(L)/(x^p)$, which agrees with
$S^jL$ in lengths $j<p$, and symmetrization is a section of
$U^{(j)}\to U^{(j)}/U^{(j-1)}$; hence $\bigoplus_{j<p}S^jL\to u(L)$ is
injective, and it is surjective in degrees $<p$ because a PBW monomial of
length $\ell$ in a graded basis of $L$ has degree $\ge\ell$. So
$\operatorname{gr}\varepsilon$ is an isomorphism and $\varepsilon$ is a strict isomorphism
of filtered spaces, which gives (1); the summand $j=1$ is $\mathfrak e$, and
$\mathrm{I}(B)^n\cap\mathfrak e=\gamma_n(\mathfrak e)$ was noted above.

(2) $J_B=\mathfrak v\cdot\mathrm{I}(B)=\sum_{j\ge1}\mathfrak v\cdot\varepsilon_j(S^j\mathfrak e)$. For
$z\in\mathfrak v$ central and $j+1\le p-1$ one has
$z\,\varepsilon_j(u_1\cdots u_j)=\varepsilon_{j+1}(zu_1\cdots u_j)$, since
$z$ may be inserted in any of the $j+1$ positions; and for $j=p-1$ the
product lies in $\mathrm{I}^2\cdot\mathrm{I}^{p-1}=0$. Stability holds because $\mathfrak v$ is an
ideal of $\mathfrak e$.

(3) As $s'=B/J_B$ and $J_B$ is a sum of subspaces of the summands with
$j\ge2$, the decomposition descends with $\mathfrak e$ intact; the filtration
statements descend because $\mathrm{I}(s')^n$ is the image of $\mathrm{I}(B)^n$ and the
decomposition is strict. Equivariance of $p_1$ is the $\operatorname{ad}(\mathfrak e)$-stability
of the summands.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Let $p$ be odd and $H$ of exponent $p$ and class $c\le p-2$. For every
$\alpha\in\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ there is $\mu\in\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H))$ such that
$\beta:=\exp(\mu)\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ lies in $\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ and $\rho(\alpha)=
\rho(\beta)$ on $V$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\hat\alpha$ be a lift of $\alpha$ to $s=s(E,V)$; it preserves
$\{V-1\}$ and $\mathrm{I}(s)^p$, hence induces an automorphism of $s'$, still written
$\hat\alpha$, with $(\hat\alpha-1)\mathrm{I}(s')\subseteq\mathrm{I}(s')^2$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:log}, $D:=\log\hat\alpha$ is a derivation of $s'$ with
$D(\mathrm{I}(s')^n)\subseteq\mathrm{I}(s')^{n+1}$ and $\hat\alpha=\exp D$; being a
polynomial in $\hat\alpha-1$, it preserves the image $\bar V$ of $\{V-1\}$
in $s'$. Now $\bar V=\{v-1:v\in V^\circ\}=\log V^\circ=\mathfrak v\subseteq\mathfrak e$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:symm}(3), and $v\mapsto v-1$ is an isomorphism
$C(V)\cong V^\circ\to\mathfrak v$ of $\mathbb{F}_p$-spaces intertwining $\rho(\alpha)$ with
$\hat\alpha|_\mathfrak v$: indeed $\{v^\alpha-1\}=\hat\alpha\{v-1\}$, and
$v^\alpha\in C(V)$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:absorb}. Hence
\[
\rho(\alpha)|_{C(V)}=\exp\bigl(D|_\mathfrak v\bigr).
\]
Put $\tilde\mu:=p_1\circ D|_\mathfrak e:\mathfrak e\to\mathfrak e$. By equivariance of $p_1$,
\[
\tilde\mu[a,b]=p_1\bigl([Da,b]+[a,Db]\bigr)=[\tilde\mu a,b]+[a,\tilde\mu b],
\]
so $\tilde\mu$ is a derivation of $\mathfrak e$; it satisfies
$\tilde\mu(\gamma_n\mathfrak e)\subseteq p_1(\mathrm{I}(s')^{n+1})\subseteq
\gamma_{n+1}(\mathfrak e)$, and $\tilde\mu|_\mathfrak v=D|_\mathfrak v$ because
$D(\mathfrak v)\subseteq\mathfrak v\subseteq\mathfrak e$ and $p_1$ is the identity on $\mathfrak e$. Let
$\mu$ be the derivation of $\mathfrak l=\mathfrak e/\mathfrak v$ induced by $\tilde\mu$; then
$\mu(\mathfrak l)\subseteq\gamma_2(\mathfrak l)$, that is $\mu\in\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l)$, and
$\tilde\mu^{c+1}=0$ since $\mathfrak e$ has class $\le c+1$.

The truncated exponentials $\exp(\mu)=\sum_{k\le c}\mu^k/k!$ and
$\exp(\tilde\mu)$ are therefore defined, and they are Lie algebra
automorphisms: expanding
$\exp(\tilde\mu)[a,b]=\sum_n\frac1{n!}\tilde\mu^n[a,b]$ by Leibniz and the
binomial identity gives $[\exp(\tilde\mu)a,\exp(\tilde\mu)b]$, all the
factorials involved being those of integers $\le c\le p-2$, hence
invertible. By the Lazard correspondence $\beta:=\exp(\mu)\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$, and
$\beta$ is the identity on $H/\gamma_2(H)$, hence on $\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2$, so
$\beta\in\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:dict}(2),
\[
\rho(\beta)|_{C(V)}=\exp(\Omega(\mu))=\exp\bigl(\tilde\mu|_\mathfrak v\bigr)
=\exp\bigl(D|_\mathfrak v\bigr)=\rho(\alpha)|_{C(V)} ,
\]
and both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ act trivially on $\mho_1(E)$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:absorb}); since $V=C(V)\oplus\mho_1(E)$, they agree
on $V$.
head: environment

label: thm:formula
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:formula}
Let $p$ be odd and $H$ of exponent $p$ and class $c\le p-2$. Then,
identifying $C(V)$ with $\mathfrak v=H_2(\mathfrak l(H))$,
\[
U(H)=\exp\Bigl(\Omega\bigl(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H))\bigr)\Bigr)\ \le\
GL\bigl(H_2(\mathfrak l(H))\bigr),\qquad
|U(H)|=p^{\,\dim\Omega(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H)))} .
\]
In particular $U(H)=1$ if and only if $\Omega(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l(H)))=0$.
head: environment
name: closed formula

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\mu\in\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l)$ we saw that $\exp(\mu)\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)\cap\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$,
and $\rho(\exp\mu)|_{C(V)}=\exp(\Omega(\mu))$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:dict}(2);
conversely every $\rho(\alpha)$ has this form by Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
With Proposition~\ref{prop:absorb} this gives $U(H)=\exp(\mathfrak u)$ for
$\mathfrak u:=\Omega(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l))$. Now $\mathfrak u$ is a Lie subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak v)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:Omega}(2)) all of whose elements raise the degree filtration
of $\mathfrak v$, which has length $\le c$; so $X^c=0$ for $X\in\mathfrak u$, and as
$c\le p-2$ the map $\exp$ is injective on $\mathfrak u$, with inverse $\log$. Hence
$|U(H)|=|\mathfrak u|$.
head: environment

label: cor:carnot
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:carnot}
Let $p$ be odd and $H$ of exponent $p$ and class $c\le p-2$, and suppose
$\mathfrak l(H)=\bigoplus_{i\ge1}\mathfrak l_i$ is graded, with $[\mathfrak l_i,\mathfrak l_j]\subseteq
\mathfrak l_{i+j}$ and generated by $\mathfrak l_1$. Then the Levi factorization holds, and
central Frattini extensions of $H$ whose small group rings are isomorphic as
pairs are isomorphic groups.
head: environment
name: graded Lazard algebras

title: Proof
body_md:
Then $\gamma_k(\mathfrak l)=\bigoplus_{i\ge k}\mathfrak l_i$ and $\operatorname{gr}\mathfrak l\cong\mathfrak l$ as graded
Lie algebras, so $L(H)=\operatorname{gr}\mathfrak l\cong\mathfrak l$. Given $\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(KH)$, the map
$\operatorname{gr}\theta$ restricts to a graded Lie automorphism of $L(H)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:grrigid}), hence to one of $\mathfrak l$, hence to some
$\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ acting on $\mathfrak l_1=L_1=\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2$ as $\theta$ does; thus
$\beta^{-1}\theta\in\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ and the Levi factorization holds. Now apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} and Lemma~\ref{lem:reform}(3).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) is Theorem~\ref{thm:main}; (2) is Theorem~\ref{thm:dict}(1),
Proposition~\ref{prop:absorb} and Theorem~\ref{thm:formula}; (3) is the last
clause of Theorem~\ref{thm:formula}; (4) is Corollary~\ref{cor:carnot}.
head: environment

label: rem:hyp
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:hyp}
The bound $c\le p-2$ enters only through Proposition~\ref{prop:E}: the
universal extension must have class $<p$ for the Lazard correspondence to
apply to it. The hypothesis of exponent $p$ enters twice, in
Proposition~\ref{prop:absorb} and in the identification of $\mathfrak e$ with a
Lie algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$. For exponent $p^2$ the logarithm of
Lemma~\ref{lem:log} still exists, but $KH/\mathrm{I}^{\,p}=K[H/D_p(H)]/\mathrm{I}^{\,p}$ sees
only the exponent-$p$ quotient, and what remains is the question of which
unipotent automorphisms of that quotient lift to $H$.
head: environment
name: the two hypotheses

label: cor:onelayer
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:onelayer}
If $\mathfrak v$ is concentrated in a single degree, then $U(H)=1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: $\Omega(\mu)$ raises the degree filtration of $\mathfrak v$, whose target is zero.
head: environment

label: ex:ladder
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:ladder}
Let $d\ge2$, $2\le c\le p-2$ and $H=F_d/\gamma_{c+1}(F_d)F_d^{\,p}$. Then
$\mathfrak l$ is the free nilpotent Lie algebra of class $c$ on $d$ generators,
$\mathfrak r=\mathfrak f_{c+1}=\ell_{c+1}(d)$ and $[\mathfrak f,\mathfrak r]=0$, so $\mathfrak v=\ell_{c+1}$ is
concentrated in degree $c+1$. Hence $U(H)=1$ and
$\dim V=\ell_{c+1}(d)+d$; and $\mathfrak l$ is graded, so by
Corollary~\ref{cor:carnot} non-isomorphic central Frattini extensions of $H$
have non-isomorphic small group rings. As $c$ and $d$ vary, these extensions
realize every nilpotency class up to $p-1$, every rank, and exponent
dividing $p^2$. The case $d=c=2$ is the extraspecial group $p^{1+2}_+$ of
order $p^3$ and exponent $p$, whose central Frattini extensions have all
orders $p^4,\dots,p^7$; it is the exact odd counterpart of $H=D_8$ at $p=2$
\cite[Ex.~6.3]{HS07}, where instead $U(H)$ is as large as the flag of $V$
allows.
head: environment
name: relatively free groups

label: prop:twogen
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:twogen}
Let $d=2$, $3\le c\le p-2$ and $N\le\gamma_c(F_2)$ with image
$\bar N\subseteq\ell_c(2)$, and put $H=F_2/\gamma_{c+1}(F_2)F_2^{\,p}N$.
Then $U(H)=1$, the Levi factorization holds, and non-isomorphic central
Frattini extensions of $H$ have non-isomorphic small group rings.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Here $\mathfrak l=\mathfrak f/\mathfrak r$ with $\mathfrak r=\bar N+\mathfrak f_{c+1}$, so $[\mathfrak f,\mathfrak r]=[\ell_1,
\bar N]$ and $\mathfrak v=\bar N\oplus\ell_{c+1}/[\ell_1,\bar N]$ lives in degrees
$c$ and $c+1$; and $\mathfrak l$ is graded. Only graded derivations of degree $1$ can
act nontrivially on $\mathfrak v$, and since $c\ge3$ gives $\mathfrak l_2=\ell_2$, such a
derivation is an arbitrary linear map $\ell_1\to\ell_2$, which extends to
$\mathfrak f$ and preserves $\mathfrak r$: thus $\operatorname{Der}_1(\mathfrak l)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\ell_1,\ell_2)$, of
dimension $2$ because $\dim\ell_2(2)=1$. The inner derivations $\operatorname{ad}_x$ with
$x\in\ell_1$ already span a $2$-dimensional subspace of it, since
$[x,\ell_1]=0$ forces $x=0$, and they lie in $\ker\Omega$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:Omega}(3)). Hence $\Omega(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l))=0$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:formula} with Corollary~\ref{cor:carnot} concludes.
head: environment

label: ex:p47
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:p47}
Let $H=\langle a,b\mid a^p,\,b^p,\,[b,a,b],\,[b,a,a,a]\rangle$, the group of
maximal class, order $p^4$ and exponent $p$. Writing $w=[y,x]$ in
$\ell(x,y)$, this is the case $c=3$, $\bar N=\langle[w,y]\rangle$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:twogen}: here $\mathfrak v_3=\langle[w,y]\rangle$ and
$\mathfrak v_4=\ell_4/\langle[[w,y],x],[[w,y],y]\rangle$ are both one-dimensional,
and for $\mu(x)=\lambda w$, $\mu(y)=\nu w$ one computes
\[
\Omega(\mu)\bigl([w,y]\bigr)=\nu\,[[w,x],y]-\lambda\,[[w,y],y]
\pmod{[\ell_1,\bar N]} .
\]
The second term lies in $[\ell_1,\bar N]$, and so does the first, by Jacobi:
$[[w,x],y]=[[w,y],x]+[w,[x,y]]=[[w,y],x]$. Thus $U(H)=1$. Here the
commutator sector of $V$ occupies two layers of the depth flag, and a
single application of the Jacobi identity replaces the computation in
$u(L(E))$ that a direct approach through the flag requires.
head: environment
name: maximal class of order $p^4$

label: thm:class2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:class2}
Let $p\ge5$ and let $H$ have class $2$ and exponent $p$. Then
$U(H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_1,L_2)/\ker\Omega$ as an elementary abelian group, every
element of $U(H)$ is realized by a central automorphism of $H$, the Levi
factorization holds, and non-isomorphic central Frattini extensions of $H$
have non-isomorphic small group rings. Moreover
$\ker\Omega\supseteq\{\omega(x,\cdot):x\in L_1\}$, so that
\[
\log_p|U(H)|\ \le\ \dim L_1\cdot\dim L_2-\dim L_1
+\dim\operatorname{rad}\omega .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:formula}, $U(H)=\exp\Omega(\operatorname{Hom}(L_1,L_2))$; and
$\Omega(\chi)^2=0$ because $\mathfrak v$ has two layers, so $\exp\Omega(\chi)=1+\Omega(\chi)$
and $U(H)$ is the additive group $\Omega(\operatorname{Hom}(L_1,L_2))$, realized by the
central automorphisms $\exp(\chi)$. The Levi factorization and the last
assertion are Corollary~\ref{cor:carnot}. Finally the inner derivation
$\operatorname{ad}_x$ restricts to $\omega(x,\cdot)$ on $L_1$ and lies in $\ker\Omega$, and
$x\mapsto\omega(x,\cdot)$ has kernel $\operatorname{rad}\omega$.
head: environment

label: ex:extraCp
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:extraCp}
Take $L_1=\langle a,b,t\rangle$, $L_2=\langle z\rangle$ with
$\omega(a,b)=z$ and $\omega(t,\cdot)=0$, so that
$K=\langle t\wedge a,\,t\wedge b\rangle$. Then $[L_1,K]$ is the part of
$\ell_3(a,b,t)$ of positive $t$-degree --- it contains $[[a,b],t]$ by Jacobi
--- so $\mathfrak v_3=\ell_3(a,b)$ has dimension $2$ and $\dim V=2+2+3=7$. For
$\chi$ with $\chi(t)=\gamma z$, formula \eqref{eq:Omclass2} gives
$\Omega(\chi)(t\wedge a)=\gamma[[a,b],a]$ and
$\Omega(\chi)(t\wedge b)=\gamma[[a,b],b]$, the contributions of $\chi(a)$ and
$\chi(b)$ having positive $t$-degree. Hence $U(H)\cong C_p$, generated by the
central automorphism $t\mapsto t[a,b]$, and the bound of
Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}, namely $3-3+1=1$, is attained.
head: environment
name: $p^{1+2}_+\times C_p$

label: prop:hd
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:hd}
Let $p\ge5$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item Let $H=(p^{1+2}_+)^M$ and write $L_1=\bigoplus_{i=1}^MU_i$ with
$\dim U_i=2$, and $L_2=\bigoplus_iZ_i$ with $Z_i=\omega(\Lambda^2U_i)$. Then
$\mathfrak v_2=K=\bigoplus_{i<j}U_i\otimes U_j$, the space
$\mathfrak v_3=\bigoplus_i\ell_3(U_i)$ has dimension $2M$, the kernel
$\ker\Omega=\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,Z_i)$ is exactly the space of inner
derivations, and $|U(H)|=p^{2M(M-1)}$.
\item For $H=\operatorname{Heis}(p^n)$, the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $SL_3(p^n)$,
$|U(H)|=p^{2n(n-1)}$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Heisenberg groups and direct powers

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) Since $\Lambda^2L_1=\bigoplus_i\Lambda^2U_i\oplus\bigoplus_{i<j}
U_i\otimes U_j$ and $\omega$ is an isomorphism on the first part and zero on
the second, $K$ is as stated. Grade $\ell_3(L_1)$ by block multidegree in
$\mathbb N^M$. The pure components are the $\ell_3(U_i)$, of dimension
$\ell_3(2)=2$ each, and every mixed component lies in $[L_1,K]$: for
$u\in U_i$ and $w\in U_j$ with $i\ne j$ one has $[u,w]\in K$, which handles
the brackets $[[u,w],y]$, while for $u,u'\in U_i$ and $w\in U_j$ the Jacobi
identity gives $[[u,u'],w]=[[u,w],u']-[[u',w],u]$. As $[L_1,K]$ is
multihomogeneous and contained in the mixed part, $\mathfrak v_3=\bigoplus_i
\ell_3(U_i)$. Now lift $\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}(L_1,L_2)$ to $\tilde\chi$ with values in
$\bigoplus_i\Lambda^2U_i$, a complement of $K$, and write $\chi_{ij}$ for
the component $U_i\to Z_j$. For $v\in U_i$ and $w\in U_j$ with $i\ne j$ only
the pure terms survive in \eqref{eq:Omclass2}:
\[
\Omega(\chi)(v\wedge w)=[\tilde\chi_{ij}(v),w]+[v,\tilde\chi_{ji}(w)]
\in\ell_3(U_j)\oplus\ell_3(U_i).
\]
The map $\Lambda^2U_j\otimes U_j\to\ell_3(U_j)$, $\zeta\otimes w\mapsto
[\zeta,w]$, is an isomorphism, both sides having dimension $2$; hence
$\Omega(\chi)=0$ if and only if $\chi_{ij}=0$ for all $i\ne j$. So
$\ker\Omega=\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,Z_i)$ has dimension $2M$ inside
$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(L_1,L_2)=2M^2$, which gives $|U(H)|=p^{2M(M-1)}$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:class2}; and the inner derivations $\omega(x,\cdot)$ with
$x=\sum_ix_i$ are precisely the maps $\bigoplus_i\omega(x_i,\cdot)$, which
fill $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(U_i,Z_i)$ because each $\omega|_{U_i}$ is
nondegenerate.

(2) Let $F=\mathbb F_{p^n}$. For $p$ odd the group $\operatorname{Heis}(F)$ is the
exponential of the strictly upper triangular $3\times3$ matrices over $F$,
so its Lazard algebra is the $3$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra
$\mathfrak h_F$ over $F$, regarded over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Every ingredient of
Theorem~\ref{thm:formula} is linear algebra compatible with extension of
scalars --- $\mathfrak v\otimes F=H_2(\mathfrak l\otimes F)$,
$\operatorname{Der}(\mathfrak l\otimes F)=\operatorname{Der}(\mathfrak l)\otimes F$ --- so
$\dim_F\Omega_F(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l\otimes F))=\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\Omega(\operatorname{Der}_{>0}(\mathfrak l))$. Since
$F\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_p}F\cong F^n$ through the Frobenius twists,
$\mathfrak l\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_p}F\cong\mathfrak h_F^{\oplus n}$ as $F$-Lie algebras, and
the computation in (1), valid over any field of odd characteristic, gives
$2n(n-1)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
So the unipotent freedom surviving in $\operatorname{Heis}(p^n)$ and in
$(p^{1+2}_+)^M$ is accounted for entirely by central automorphisms, and its
size counts the ``off-diagonal'' ones; for $M=1$ it recovers
$U(p^{1+2}_+)=1$. Note that Theorem~\ref{thm:class2} assumes nothing about
$\omega$ beyond surjectivity, so it covers every semifield group
\cite{Ver87}, and in particular the families of \cite{LW12}.
head: environment

label: prob:levi
title: Problem
body_md:
\label{prob:levi}
Does $\operatorname{Aut}(KH)=\operatorname{Aut}(H)\cdot\operatorname{UAut}(KH)$ hold for every $H$ of exponent $p$ and
class $\le p-2$? Equivalently, is the image of $\operatorname{Aut}(KH)$ in
$GL(H/\Phi(H))$ contained in that of $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathfrak l(H))$? By
Corollary~\ref{cor:carnot} this holds whenever $\mathfrak l(H)$ is graded, and it is
the only hypothesis remaining in the conclusion about small group rings in
exponent $p$.
head: environment
name: Levi factorization

label: prob:ceiling
title: Problem
body_md:
\label{prob:ceiling}
Extend Theorem~\ref{thm:main} to class $c=p-1$. For
$H=F_d/\gamma_p(F_d)F_d^{\,p}$ the commutator sector of $V$ collapses into
depth $p$ and $U(H)=1$ follows from the flag alone, so the residual
configuration is that in which $H_2(\mathfrak l)$ is spread over at least three
degrees with top degree $p$, where it becomes invisible in
$s/\mathrm{I}^{\,p}$; the smallest instance is $p=5$, $c=4$, $d\ge3$, the case
$d=2$ being excluded as in Proposition~\ref{prop:twogen}.
head: environment
name: the ceiling

title: Problem
body_md:
For $H$ of class $2$ and exponent $p$, describe $\ker\Omega$ in terms of
$\omega$. Proposition~\ref{prop:hd} shows that it consists exactly of the
inner derivations when $\omega$ is an orthogonal sum of hyperbolic planes
with independent value lines; for which $\omega$ is this the case, and for
which is $U(H)=1$?
head: environment
name: the kernel of $\Om$
